h: Up the Trees, Then Up to Solomon's Temple
p: If your legs still work after the zip wires, there's a classic little Buxton walk waiting right next door. From the Poole's Cavern side of the country park you can follow the path up through the woods to Solomon's Temple, the stubby Victorian tower on top of Grin Low. Climb the steps inside and you get a lovely view back over the town and out across the Peak, which is a nice way to see how far you've come in one day.

Timing helps here. A treetop session takes a couple of hours, so a morning slot leaves the afternoon free for the cavern, the walk or a mooch around town. In summer, an early slot also means cooler air under the trees.

Down in Buxton, it's worth seeking out St Ann's Well near The Crescent, where spring water still flows from the tap and locals fill their bottles. The Buxton Opera House, a gorgeous Edwardian theatre, puts on shows all year if you fancy an evening out, and the town's annual festival brings in music, books and comedy over the summer.

Buxton also makes a smart base for a longer Peak District break. Castleton's show caves and Mam Tor are within reasonable driving distance, and Chatsworth is an easy day trip too. Pack a flask, a spare pair of socks and a waterproof, and you'll be ready for whatever the hills decide to throw at you.
